name: Terry Lau
life: “I still remember saying no to my child at a bank counter.” People around Paper & Pine Books know Terry by a small Tuesday habit. Terry starts with the handwritten shelf cards and often leaves with a suggestion for somebody else.
voice: I declined to be a guarantor for my own child. I'm helping this mother find a way to say yes with limits.
appearance: Terry has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Look for a gray streak running back from the forehead. Out of work clothes, the familiar outfit is a plum-colored cardigan with a pen clipped inside the neckline. In conversation Terry rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Terry enjoys bargaining, including over things already settled. It is partly a joke and partly a test of whether the other person feels able to say no.
agenda: To help the mother set a limit without taking over.
family: Elias Hart is Terry’s younger cousin. Terry chooses whether to use it. Elias saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The almost scholarship*, Elias says, “I found a host family. They have an empty room and a curfew the winner's evening job can't meet.”
connections: Grant Penn. The carer and another parent compare what helping somebody can cost other family members.

reactions.situation: A sibling wants the bank figures read at a family meal
reactions.response: Terry asks the guarantor what can be shared at dinner before reading out any figures.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Terry takes a small plate to the quieter end of the table and saves the seat beside it.
